# Page: System Setup and Configuration

# System Setup and Configuration

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/setup.jl](src/setup.jl)

</details>



This document covers the initialization and configuration of molecular dynamics systems in Molly.jl. It explains how to create `System` objects from coordinate files, force field definitions, and topology information, as well as utility functions for generating initial configurations. For information about the core `System` data structure itself, see [System and Atoms](#3.1). For details about force field file formats and file I/O operations, see [Force Fields and File I/O](#7.1).

## System Creation Overview

The system setup process in Molly.jl centers around creating `System` objects that contain all the information needed for molecular dynamics simulations. The main entry point is through `System` constructors that can read various file formats.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input Sources"
        CoordFile["Coordinate File<br/>(PDB, XYZ, etc.)"]
        FFFile["Force Field File<br/>(OpenMM XML)"]
        TopFile["Topology File<br/>(Gromacs)"]
        GenCoords["Generated Coordinates<br/>(place_atoms, place_diatomics)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Parsing and Processing"
        MolFF["MolecularForceField<br/>Constructor"]
        ChemFiles["Chemfiles.jl<br/>File Reading"]
        TopParser["Gromacs Topology<br/>Parser"]
        CoordGen["Coordinate<br/>Generation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "System Components"
        Atoms["Atom[]<br/>atom data"]
        Coords["Coordinates<br/>positions"]
        Boundary["Boundary<br/>box definition"]
        PairInter["Pairwise Interactions<br/>(LJ, Coulomb)"]
        SpecInter["Specific Interactions<br/>(bonds, angles, torsions)"]
        NeighFinder["Neighbor Finder<br/>configuration"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Final System"
        SysObj["System Object<br/>Complete MD system"]
    end
    
    CoordFile --> ChemFiles
    FFFile --> MolFF
    TopFile --> TopParser
    GenCoords --> CoordGen
    
    ChemFiles --> Atoms
    ChemFiles --> Coords
    ChemFiles --> Boundary
    
    MolFF --> PairInter
    MolFF --> SpecInter
    
    TopParser --> Atoms
    TopParser --> SpecInter
    TopParser --> Coords
    
    CoordGen --> Coords
    
    Atoms --> SysObj
    Coords --> SysObj
    Boundary --> SysObj
    PairInter --> SysObj
    SpecInter --> SysObj
    NeighFinder --> SysObj
```

Sources: [src/setup.jl:471-1009](), [src/setup.jl:1011-1403]()

## Force Field Definition

The `MolecularForceField` type serves as the central container for all force field parameters. It is constructed by parsing OpenMM XML force field files.

| Component | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `atom_types` | `Dict{String, AtomType}` | Atom type definitions with σ, ϵ, mass, charge |
| `residue_types` | `Dict{String, ResidueType}` | Residue templates with atom mappings |
| `bond_types` | `Dict{Tuple{String, String}, HarmonicBond}` | Bond parameter definitions |
| `angle_types` | `Dict{Tuple{String, String, String}, HarmonicAngle}` | Angle parameter definitions |
| `torsion_types` | `Dict{Tuple{String, String, String, String}, PeriodicTorsionType}` | Torsion parameter definitions |

The force field constructor parses various XML sections:

- **AtomTypes**: Defines basic atom properties [src/setup.jl:209-220]()
- **Residues**: Maps atom names to types within residues [src/setup.jl:221-245]()
- **HarmonicBondForce**: Bond parameters [src/setup.jl:246-257]()
- **HarmonicAngleForce**: Angle parameters [src/setup.jl:258-270]()
- **PeriodicTorsionForce**: Torsion parameters [src/setup.jl:271-297]()
- **NonbondedForce**: Lennard-Jones and electrostatic parameters [src/setup.jl:298-344]()

Sources: [src/setup.jl:171-378]()

## System Construction Process

The `System` constructor follows a detailed process to build complete molecular systems from input files:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "File Reading Phase"
        ReadCoord["Read Coordinate File<br/>(Chemfiles.Trajectory)"]
        ReadTop["Extract Topology<br/>(bonds, angles, dihedrals)"]
        ParseRes["Parse Residues<br/>(residue_name, terminal handling)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Atom Processing"
        CreateAtoms["Create Atom Objects<br/>(mass, charge, σ, ϵ)"]
        CreateAtomData["Create AtomData<br/>(names, types, residues)"]
        HandleTerminal["Handle Terminal Residues<br/>(NMET, CMET, etc.)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Interaction Setup"
        BuildBonds["Build Bond Lists<br/>(InteractionList2Atoms)"]
        BuildAngles["Build Angle Lists<br/>(InteractionList3Atoms)"]
        BuildTorsions["Build Torsion Lists<br/>(InteractionList4Atoms)"]
        BuildImpropers["Build Improper Lists<br/>(wildcard matching)"]
        SetupNonbonded["Setup Nonbonded<br/>(LennardJones, Coulomb)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "System Assembly"
        SetupNeighbors["Configure NeighborFinder<br/>(eligible, special matrices)"]
        SetupBoundary["Setup Boundary Conditions<br/>(from file or specified)"]
        CreateSystem["Assemble System Object<br/>(all components)"]
    end
    
    ReadCoord --> CreateAtoms
    ReadTop --> BuildBonds
    ParseRes --> CreateAtomData
    
    CreateAtoms --> HandleTerminal
    HandleTerminal --> BuildBonds
    BuildBonds --> BuildAngles
    BuildAngles --> BuildTorsions
    BuildTorsions --> BuildImpropers
    BuildImpropers --> SetupNonbonded
    
    SetupNonbonded --> SetupNeighbors
    SetupNeighbors --> SetupBoundary
    SetupBoundary --> CreateSystem
```

Sources: [src/setup.jl:471-1009]()

### Coordinate Processing

Coordinates are read using Chemfiles.jl and undergo several processing steps:

1. **File Reading**: `Chemfiles.Trajectory` reads various formats [src/setup.jl:493-496]()
2. **Unit Conversion**: Conversion from Ångström to nanometer [src/setup.jl:918-922]()
3. **Coordinate Centering**: Optional centering in simulation box [src/setup.jl:923-925]()
4. **Boundary Wrapping**: Ensure coordinates are within periodic boundaries [src/setup.jl:926]()

### Topology Construction

The system automatically builds interaction lists from the molecular topology:

- **Bond Detection**: From `Chemfiles.bonds()` or topology file [src/setup.jl:604-623]()
- **Angle Detection**: From `Chemfiles.angles()` [src/setup.jl:625-648]()
- **Torsion Handling**: Includes wildcard matching for force field types [src/setup.jl:650-713]()
- **Improper Handling**: Complex matching with permutation rules [src/setup.jl:716-819]()

Sources: [src/setup.jl:508-819]()

## Configuration Options

The `System` constructor accepts numerous configuration options:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `boundary` | `nothing` | Simulation box (read from file if `nothing`) |
| `velocities` | `nothing` | Initial velocities (zero if `nothing`) |
| `units` | `true` | Whether to use Unitful.jl quantities |
| `array_type` | `Array` | Array backend (`CuArray`, `ROCArray`, etc.) |
| `dist_cutoff` | `1.0u"nm"` | Cutoff for long-range interactions |
| `dist_neighbors` | `1.2u"nm"` | Neighbor list cutoff distance |
| `center_coords` | `true` | Whether to center coordinates in box |
| `neighbor_finder_type` | `nothing` | Specific neighbor finder implementation |
| `implicit_solvent` | `nothing` | Implicit solvent model ("obc1", "obc2", "gbn2") |
| `rename_terminal_res` | `true` | Rename terminal residues (e.g., "MET" → "NMET") |

Sources: [src/setup.jl:471-485]()

### Neighbor Finder Selection

The system automatically selects appropriate neighbor finders based on the array type:

```mermaid
graph TD
    ArrayType{"Array Type<br/>Specified"}
    
    CPUGPU{"CPU or GPU<br/>Backend?"}
    CUDACheck{"CUDA<br/>Compatible?"}
    
    CellListMap["CellListMapNeighborFinder<br/>(CPU default)"]
    GPUNeighbor["GPUNeighborFinder<br/>(CUDA optimized)"]
    DistanceNeighbor["DistanceNeighborFinder<br/>(non-CUDA GPU)"]
    NoNeighbor["NoNeighborFinder<br/>(explicit specification)"]
    
    ArrayType --> CPUGPU
    CPUGPU -->|CPU| CellListMap
    CPUGPU -->|GPU| CUDACheck
    CUDACheck -->|Yes| GPUNeighbor
    CUDACheck -->|No| DistanceNeighbor
    ArrayType -->|NoNeighborFinder| NoNeighbor
```

Sources: [src/setup.jl:928-960]()

## Coordinate Generation Utilities

Molly.jl provides utilities for generating initial coordinate configurations:

### `place_atoms` Function

Generates random atomic coordinates with minimum distance constraints:

```julia
place_atoms(n_atoms, boundary; min_dist=0.0, max_attempts=100, rng=default_rng())
```

- Ensures no two atoms are closer than `min_dist`
- Accounts for periodic boundary conditions
- Fails after `max_attempts` placement attempts

Sources: [src/setup.jl:16-64]()

### `place_diatomics` Function

Generates coordinates for diatomic molecules:

```julia
place_diatomics(n_molecules, boundary, bond_length; 
                min_dist=0.0, max_attempts=100, aligned=false, rng=default_rng())
```

- Creates pairs of atoms separated by `bond_length`
- Optional alignment control via `aligned` parameter
- Maintains minimum distance between all atoms

Sources: [src/setup.jl:66-129]()

## System Modification Utilities

### Position Restraints

The `add_position_restraints` function adds harmonic restraints to existing systems:

```julia
add_position_restraints(sys, k; atom_selector=is_any_atom, restrain_coords=sys.coords)
```

- `k`: Force constant (scalar or per-atom array)
- `atom_selector`: Function to determine which atoms to restrain
- Built-in selectors: `is_any_atom`, `is_heavy_atom`

The function creates `HarmonicPositionRestraint` interactions and returns a modified system copy.

Sources: [src/setup.jl:1425-1477]()

### Atom Selection Functions

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `is_any_atom` | Selects all atoms (placeholder function) |
| `is_heavy_atom` | Selects non-hydrogen atoms based on mass or element |

Sources: [src/setup.jl:1405-1423]()

# Page: Force Fields and File I/O

# Force Fields and File I/O

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/setup.jl](src/setup.jl)

</details>



This page covers the loading and parsing of molecular force fields from XML files and the reading of coordinate data to set up molecular systems. It focuses on the file I/O capabilities that allow Molly.jl to interface with standard molecular simulation file formats, particularly OpenMM force field XML files and various coordinate formats supported by Chemfiles.

For information about the `System` data structure itself, see [System and Atoms](#3.1). For details about how interactions are calculated once loaded, see [Interaction System](#4). For unit handling in file I/O, see [Units and Physical Quantities](#7.2).

## Overview of Force Field and File I/O System

Molly.jl provides comprehensive support for reading molecular systems from files, with two main pathways for system setup:

```mermaid
graph TD
    XMLFiles["OpenMM XML Files<br/>(.xml)"] --> MFF["MolecularForceField"]
    CoordFiles["Coordinate Files<br/>(PDB, XYZ, etc.)"] --> System["System"]
    MFF --> System
    
    GromacsTOP["Gromacs Topology<br/>(.top)"] --> System
    GromacsGRO["Gromacs Coordinates<br/>(.gro)"] --> System
    
    RandomCoords["place_atoms()<br/>place_diatomics()"] --> System
    
    System --> Simulation["Ready for Simulation"]
    
    style MFF fill:#f9f9f9
    style System fill:#e1f5fe
```

The system supports two primary workflows: the OpenMM-compatible pathway using XML force fields with Chemfiles-readable coordinate formats, and the Gromacs pathway reading native Gromacs topology and coordinate files.

Sources: [src/setup.jl:1-1478]()

## Force Field Data Structures

### MolecularForceField

The `MolecularForceField` type serves as the central container for all force field parameters parsed from OpenMM XML files:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "MolecularForceField Components"
        AtomTypes["atom_types<br/>Dict{String, AtomType}"]
        ResidueTypes["residue_types<br/>Dict{String, ResidueType}"] 
        BondTypes["bond_types<br/>Dict{Tuple, HarmonicBond}"]
        AngleTypes["angle_types<br/>Dict{Tuple, HarmonicAngle}"]
        TorsionTypes["torsion_types<br/>Dict{Tuple, PeriodicTorsionType}"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Force Field Parameters"
        Weights["weight_14_coulomb<br/>weight_14_lj"]
        Order["torsion_order"]
        Attributes["attributes_from_residue"]
    end
    
    AtomTypes --> MFF["MolecularForceField"]
    ResidueTypes --> MFF
    BondTypes --> MFF
    AngleTypes --> MFF
    TorsionTypes --> MFF
    Weights --> MFF
    Order --> MFF
    Attributes --> MFF
```

The `AtomType` struct contains fundamental atomic parameters:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `type` | `String` | Atom type identifier |
| `class` | `String` | Atom class (currently unused) |
| `element` | `String` | Chemical element symbol |
| `charge` | `Union{T, Missing}` | Partial charge |
| `mass` | `M` | Atomic mass |
| `σ` | `S` | Lennard-Jones sigma parameter |
| `ϵ` | `E` | Lennard-Jones epsilon parameter |

Sources: [src/setup.jl:136-144](), [src/setup.jl:181-191]()

### XML Parsing Process

The force field XML parsing follows OpenMM conventions and extracts parameters for different interaction types:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    XMLFile["OpenMM XML File"] --> Parser["parsexml()"]
    Parser --> Root["Root Element"]
    
    Root --> AtomTypesSection["AtomTypes Section"]
    Root --> ResiduesSection["Residues Section"] 
    Root --> BondForceSection["HarmonicBondForce Section"]
    Root --> AngleForceSection["HarmonicAngleForce Section"]
    Root --> TorsionForceSection["PeriodicTorsionForce Section"]
    Root --> NonbondedSection["NonbondedForce Section"]
    
    AtomTypesSection --> ParseAtomTypes["Parse Atom Types<br/>(name, class, element, mass)"]
    ResiduesSection --> ParseResidues["Parse Residues<br/>(atom assignments, charges)"]
    BondForceSection --> ParseBonds["Parse Bond Parameters<br/>(k, length)"]
    AngleForceSection --> ParseAngles["Parse Angle Parameters<br/>(k, angle)"]
    TorsionForceSection --> ParseTorsions["Parse Torsion Parameters<br/>(periodicities, phases, ks)"]
    NonbondedSection --> ParseNonbonded["Parse LJ Parameters<br/>(sigma, epsilon, charges)"]
    
    ParseAtomTypes --> MFF["MolecularForceField"]
    ParseResidues --> MFF
    ParseBonds --> MFF
    ParseAngles --> MFF
    ParseTorsions --> MFF
    ParseNonbonded --> MFF
```

Sources: [src/setup.jl:204-356]()

## System Construction from Files

### OpenMM-Style System Construction

The primary `System` constructor reads coordinate files and applies force field parameters:

```mermaid
graph TD
    CoordFile["Coordinate File<br/>(PDB, XYZ, etc.)"] --> Chemfiles["Chemfiles.Trajectory"]
    FF["MolecularForceField"] --> SystemConstructor["System Constructor"]
    Chemfiles --> SystemConstructor
    
    SystemConstructor --> ParseTopology["Parse Topology<br/>(bonds, angles, dihedrals)"]
    SystemConstructor --> ParseCoords["Parse Coordinates<br/>(positions, boundary)"]
    SystemConstructor --> MatchTypes["Match Atom Types<br/>(residue templates)"]
    
    ParseTopology --> BuildInteractions["Build Interaction Lists<br/>(bonds, angles, torsions)"]
    MatchTypes --> BuildAtoms["Build Atom Arrays<br/>(charges, masses, LJ params)"]
    ParseCoords --> ProcessCoords["Process Coordinates<br/>(center, wrap)"]
    
    BuildInteractions --> FinalSystem["System"]
    BuildAtoms --> FinalSystem
    ProcessCoords --> FinalSystem
    
    FinalSystem --> SetupNeighbors["Setup Neighbor Finder"]
    FinalSystem --> SetupSolvent["Setup Implicit Solvent<br/>(optional)"]
```

The constructor performs several key operations:

1. **Topology Analysis**: Extracts bonds, angles, and dihedrals from the coordinate file using Chemfiles
2. **Residue Matching**: Matches atoms to force field residue templates by name
3. **Parameter Assignment**: Applies force field parameters to create interaction objects
4. **Coordinate Processing**: Centers and wraps coordinates according to boundary conditions

Sources: [src/setup.jl:471-1009]()

### Gromacs File Support

Molly.jl also supports reading Gromacs topology and coordinate files directly:

```mermaid
graph LR
    TopFile[".top File"] --> ParseSections["Parse Sections<br/>[atomtypes], [bonds], etc."]
    GroFile[".gro File"] --> ParseCoords["Parse Coordinates<br/>and Box Dimensions"]
    
    ParseSections --> BuildFF["Build Force Field<br/>Parameters"]
    ParseCoords --> BuildCoords["Build Coordinate<br/>Arrays"]
    
    BuildFF --> System["System"]
    BuildCoords --> System
```

The Gromacs reader processes topology sections sequentially:

| Section | Purpose | Data Extracted |
|---------|---------|----------------|
| `[atomtypes]` | Atom type definitions | Mass, charge, σ, ϵ |
| `[atoms]` | Atom assignments | Type mapping, charges |
| `[bonds]` | Bond definitions | Harmonic bond parameters |
| `[angles]` | Angle definitions | Harmonic angle parameters |
| `[dihedrals]` | Torsion definitions | RB torsion parameters |
| `[pairs]` | 1-4 interactions | Special pair listings |

Sources: [src/setup.jl:1011-1399]()

## Interaction List Construction

### Topology Processing

The system construction process builds interaction lists by matching atomic connectivity to force field parameters:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    TopologyData["Topology from File<br/>(bonds, angles, dihedrals)"] --> MatchParameters["Match to Force Field Parameters"]
    
    subgraph "Bond Processing"
        BondPairs["Bond Pairs<br/>(atom1, atom2)"] --> LookupBondType["Lookup Bond Type<br/>in force_field.bond_types"]
        LookupBondType --> CreateBond["Create HarmonicBond<br/>(k, r0)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Angle Processing"  
        AngleTriplets["Angle Triplets<br/>(atom1, atom2, atom3)"] --> LookupAngleType["Lookup Angle Type<br/>in force_field.angle_types"]
        LookupAngleType --> CreateAngle["Create HarmonicAngle<br/>(k, θ0)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Torsion Processing"
        TorsionQuads["Torsion Quartets<br/>(atom1, atom2, atom3, atom4)"] --> WildcardSearch["Wildcard Search<br/>in force_field.torsion_types"]
        WildcardSearch --> CreateTorsion["Create PeriodicTorsion<br/>(periodicities, phases, ks)"]
    end
    
    MatchParameters --> BondPairs
    MatchParameters --> AngleTriplets  
    MatchParameters --> TorsionQuads
    
    CreateBond --> InteractionLists["InteractionList2Atoms<br/>InteractionList3Atoms<br/>InteractionList4Atoms"]
    CreateAngle --> InteractionLists
    CreateTorsion --> InteractionLists
```

The torsion parameter matching uses a sophisticated wildcard system where empty strings in the force field type keys act as wildcards, allowing flexible parameter assignment.

Sources: [src/setup.jl:604-818]()

### Special Topology Handling

The system handles several special cases during topology construction:

1. **N-terminal Residues**: Automatically adds missing hydrogen bonds and angles for N-terminal amino acids
2. **Water Molecules**: Adds missing O-H bonds and H-O-H angles for HOH residues  
3. **Terminal Residue Renaming**: Modifies residue names (e.g., "MET" → "NMET") to match appropriate force field templates

```mermaid
graph TD
    ResidueAnalysis["Analyze Residues"] --> CheckStandard{"Standard Residue?"}
    CheckStandard -->|Yes| CheckTerminal{"Terminal Position?"}
    CheckStandard -->|No| CheckWater{"Water (HOH)?"}
    
    CheckTerminal -->|N-terminal| AddNtermBonds["Add N-terminal H bonds<br/>and angles"]
    CheckTerminal -->|C-terminal| AddCtermBonds["Add C-terminal bonds"]
    CheckTerminal -->|Internal| StandardProcessing["Standard Processing"]
    
    CheckWater -->|Yes| AddWaterBonds["Add O-H bonds<br/>and H-O-H angle"]
    CheckWater -->|No| StandardProcessing
    
    AddNtermBonds --> ContinueProcessing["Continue Processing"]
    AddCtermBonds --> ContinueProcessing
    AddWaterBonds --> ContinueProcessing
    StandardProcessing --> ContinueProcessing
```

Sources: [src/setup.jl:521-565]()

## Coordinate and Random Placement

### File-based Coordinate Reading

Coordinate files are read using the Chemfiles library, which supports numerous formats:

```mermaid
graph LR
    ChemfilesFormats["Supported Formats<br/>PDB, XYZ, DCD, TRR, etc."] --> ChemfilesReader["Chemfiles.Trajectory"]
    ChemfilesReader --> ExtractData["Extract Positions<br/>and Unit Cell"]
    ExtractData --> ConvertUnits["Convert Å → nm"]
    ConvertUnits --> ProcessCoords["Center and Wrap<br/>Coordinates"]
    ProcessCoords --> SystemCoords["System.coords"]
```

The coordinate processing includes automatic unit conversion from Ångströms to nanometers and optional coordinate centering within the simulation box.

Sources: [src/setup.jl:917-926]()

### Random Coordinate Generation

For system initialization without coordinate files, Molly.jl provides functions to generate random atomic positions:

| Function | Purpose | Key Parameters |
|----------|---------|----------------|
| `place_atoms` | Random monatomic placement | `n_atoms`, `boundary`, `min_dist` |
| `place_diatomics` | Random diatomic molecules | `n_molecules`, `bond_length`, `aligned` |

Both functions ensure minimum distance constraints and account for periodic boundary conditions.

```mermaid
graph TD
    RandomPlacement["Random Placement Request"] --> CheckBoundary{"Finite Boundary?"}
    CheckBoundary -->|No| ThrowError["Throw ArgumentError"]
    CheckBoundary -->|Yes| CalculateMaxAtoms["Calculate Maximum<br/>Possible Atoms"]
    
    CalculateMaxAtoms --> CheckFeasibility{"n_atoms ≤ max_atoms?"}
    CheckFeasibility -->|No| ThrowError
    CheckFeasibility -->|Yes| PlacementLoop["Placement Loop"]
    
    PlacementLoop --> GenerateCoord["Generate Random<br/>Coordinate"]
    GenerateCoord --> CheckMinDist{"Min Distance<br/>Satisfied?"}
    CheckMinDist -->|Yes| AcceptCoord["Accept Coordinate"]
    CheckMinDist -->|No| IncrementAttempts["Increment Failed<br/>Attempts"]
    
    IncrementAttempts --> CheckMaxAttempts{"Max Attempts<br/>Reached?"}
    CheckMaxAttempts -->|Yes| ThrowError
    CheckMaxAttempts -->|No| PlacementLoop
    
    AcceptCoord --> CheckComplete{"All Atoms<br/>Placed?"}
    CheckComplete -->|No| PlacementLoop
    CheckComplete -->|Yes| ReturnCoords["Return Coordinates"]
```

Sources: [src/setup.jl:27-129]()

## Position Restraints and System Modification

### Adding Position Restraints

The `add_position_restraints` function demonstrates how to modify existing systems by adding new interaction types:

```mermaid
graph LR
    ExistingSystem["Existing System"] --> SelectAtoms["Select Atoms<br/>(atom_selector function)"]
    RestraintParams["Force Constants<br/>(k values)"] --> SelectAtoms
    ReferenceCoords["Reference Coordinates<br/>(restrain_coords)"] --> SelectAtoms
    
    SelectAtoms --> CreateRestraints["Create HarmonicPositionRestraint<br/>objects"]
    CreateRestraints --> BuildInteractionList["Build InteractionList1Atoms"]
    BuildInteractionList --> AddToSystem["Add to specific_inter_lists"]
    AddToSystem --> ModifiedSystem["Modified System"]
```

The function supports flexible atom selection through callback functions like `is_heavy_atom` and `is_any_atom`.

Sources: [src/setup.jl:1437-1477]()

# Page: Units and Physical Quantities

# Units and Physical Quantities

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/Project.toml](docs/Project.toml)
- [docs/make.jl](docs/make.jl)
- [docs/src/index.md](docs/src/index.md)
- [src/units.jl](src/units.jl)

</details>



This page covers how Molly.jl handles physical units and quantities using Unitful.jl. It explains the unit validation system, consistency requirements, and supported unit types for molecular dynamics simulations.

For information about system initialization and configuration, see [System Setup and Configuration](#7). For details on force field parameters and their units, see [Force Fields and File I/O](#7.1).

## Overview

Molly.jl integrates with Unitful.jl to provide comprehensive unit handling for molecular dynamics simulations. The package enforces strict unit consistency throughout the system to prevent physics errors and ensure meaningful calculations. All physical quantities must have compatible units, and the system validates unit consistency during initialization.

The unit system supports both molar and non-molar quantities, allowing users to work with traditional molecular dynamics units (e.g., `kcal/mol`) or absolute units (e.g., `kcal`). However, mixing molar and non-molar units within a single system is not permitted.

Sources: [src/units.jl:1-214]()

## Unit Types and Dimensions

### Unit Types and Their Relationships

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Primary Units"
        Length["Length Units<br/>(𝐋)<br/>Examples: nm, Å, m"]
        Mass["Mass Units<br/>(𝐌)<br/>Examples: kg, u"]
        Time["Time Units<br/>(𝐓)<br/>Examples: ps, fs, s"]
        Temperature["Temperature Units<br/>(𝚯)<br/>Examples: K"]
        Amount["Amount Units<br/>(𝐍)<br/>Examples: mol"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Derived Units"
        Velocity["Velocity Units<br/>(𝐋⋅𝐓⁻¹)<br/>Examples: nm/ps, m/s"]
        Energy["Energy Units<br/>(𝐋²⋅𝐌⋅𝐓⁻²)<br/>Examples: kJ, kcal"]
        Force["Force Units<br/>(𝐋⋅𝐌⋅𝐓⁻²)<br/>Examples: kJ/nm, N"]
        MolarEnergy["Molar Energy<br/>(𝐋²⋅𝐌⋅𝐓⁻²⋅𝐍⁻¹)<br/>Examples: kJ/mol, kcal/mol"]
        MolarMass["Molar Mass<br/>(𝐌⋅𝐍⁻¹)<br/>Examples: kg/mol, g/mol"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Special Constants"
        BoltzmannConst["Boltzmann Constant<br/>(𝐋²⋅𝐌⋅𝐓⁻²⋅𝚯⁻¹)<br/>k"]
        MolarBoltzmann["Molar Boltzmann<br/>(𝐋²⋅𝐌⋅𝐓⁻²⋅𝚯⁻¹⋅𝐍⁻¹)<br/>k⋅Nₐ"]
    end
    
    Length --> Velocity
    Time --> Velocity
    Length --> Energy
    Mass --> Energy
    Time --> Energy
    Energy --> Force
    Length --> Force
    Energy --> MolarEnergy
    Amount --> MolarEnergy
    Mass --> MolarMass
    Amount --> MolarMass
    
    Energy --> BoltzmannConst
    Temperature --> BoltzmannConst
    BoltzmannConst --> MolarBoltzmann
    Amount --> MolarBoltzmann
    
    style Energy fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style Force fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style MolarEnergy fill:#bbf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style MolarMass fill:#bbf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

Molly.jl defines several derived dimensions for molecular dynamics calculations. The system recognizes both molar and non-molar variants of energy and mass units, with strict consistency enforcement between related quantities.

Sources: [src/units.jl:6-8](), [src/units.jl:92-96](), [src/units.jl:105-111]()

### Supported Unit Dimensions

| Quantity | Valid Dimensions | Examples | Notes |
|----------|------------------|----------|--------|
| Length | `𝐋`, `NoDims` | `1.0u"nm"`, `1.0` | All coordinates must use same units |
| Velocity | `𝐋⋅𝐓⁻¹`, `NoDims` | `1.0u"nm/ps"`, `1.0` | Derived from length and time |
| Mass | `𝐌`, `𝐌⋅𝐍⁻¹`, `NoDims` | `1.0u"kg"`, `1.0u"kg/mol"`, `1.0` | Atomic or molar mass |
| Energy | `𝐋²⋅𝐌⋅𝐓⁻²`, `𝐋²⋅𝐌⋅𝐓⁻²⋅𝐍⁻¹`, `NoDims` | `1.0u"kJ"`, `1.0u"kJ/mol"`, `1.0` | Absolute or molar energy |
| Force | `𝐋⋅𝐌⋅𝐓⁻²`, `𝐋⋅𝐌⋅𝐓⁻²⋅𝐍⁻¹`, `NoDims` | `1.0u"kJ/nm"`, `1.0u"kJ/(mol⋅nm)"`, `1.0` | Derived from energy/length |

Sources: [src/units.jl:125-131](), [src/units.jl:145-151](), [src/units.jl:105-111](), [src/units.jl:92-96]()

## Unit Validation System

### Validation Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    SystemInit["System Initialization"]
    CheckUnits["check_units()"]
    CheckSystemUnits["check_system_units()"]
    CheckOtherUnits["check_other_units()"]
    
    subgraph "System Unit Validation"
        ValidateCoords["validate_coords()"]
        ValidateVels["validate_velocities()"]
        ValidateMasses["validate_masses()"]
        ValidateEnergy["validate_energy_units()"]
        CheckConsistency["Check Molar Consistency"]
        CheckDerivation["Check Force = Energy/Length"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Other Unit Validation"
        ValidateBoundary["Validate Boundary Units"]
        ValidateAtomParams["Validate Atom σ, ϵ Units"]
    end
    
    Success["Return sys_units NamedTuple"]
    Error["Throw ArgumentError"]
    
    SystemInit --> CheckUnits
    CheckUnits --> CheckSystemUnits
    CheckUnits --> CheckOtherUnits
    
    CheckSystemUnits --> ValidateCoords
    CheckSystemUnits --> ValidateVels
    CheckSystemUnits --> ValidateMasses
    CheckSystemUnits --> ValidateEnergy
    CheckSystemUnits --> CheckConsistency
    CheckSystemUnits --> CheckDerivation
    
    CheckOtherUnits --> ValidateBoundary
    CheckOtherUnits --> ValidateAtomParams
    
    ValidateCoords --> Success
    ValidateVels --> Success
    ValidateMasses --> Success
    ValidateEnergy --> Success
    CheckConsistency --> Success
    CheckDerivation --> Success
    ValidateBoundary --> Success
    ValidateAtomParams --> Success
    
    ValidateCoords --> Error
    ValidateVels --> Error
    ValidateMasses --> Error
    ValidateEnergy --> Error
    CheckConsistency --> Error
    CheckDerivation --> Error
    ValidateBoundary --> Error
    ValidateAtomParams --> Error
    
    style CheckUnits fill:#e1f5fe
    style Success fill:#e8f5e8
    style Error fill:#ffebee
```

The unit validation system performs comprehensive checks during system initialization. The main entry point `check_units()` coordinates validation of system units and cross-checks with other components like boundary conditions and atom parameters.

Sources: [src/units.jl:20-26](), [src/units.jl:28-63](), [src/units.jl:65-89]()

### Consistency Requirements

The system enforces several critical consistency rules:

1. **Molar Consistency**: All quantities must be either molar, non-molar, or unitless. Mixing is not allowed.
2. **Unit Homogeneity**: All atoms must have the same mass units, all coordinates must have the same length units.
3. **Derived Unit Relationships**: Force units must equal energy units divided by length units.
4. **No Mixed Dimensionality**: Cannot mix dimensioned and dimensionless quantities.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Molar Consistency Check"
        EnergyMolar["energy_is_molar<br/>(𝐋²⋅𝐌⋅𝐍⁻¹⋅𝐓⁻²)"]
        ForceMolar["force_is_molar<br/>(𝐋⋅𝐌⋅𝐍⁻¹⋅𝐓⁻²)"]
        MassMolar["mass_is_molar<br/>(𝐌⋅𝐍⁻¹)"]
        AllMatch["All Must Match"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Derived Unit Check"
        ForceUnits["force_units"]
        EnergyUnits["energy_units"]
        LengthUnits["length_units"]
        Relationship["force_units == energy_units / length_units"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Dimensionality Check"
        NoDimensions["Any quantity has NoDims"]
        AllNoDims["All quantities must have NoDims"]
    end
    
    EnergyMolar --> AllMatch
    ForceMolar --> AllMatch
    MassMolar --> AllMatch
    
    ForceUnits --> Relationship
    EnergyUnits --> Relationship
    LengthUnits --> Relationship
    
    NoDimensions --> AllNoDims
    
    style AllMatch fill:#fff3e0
    style Relationship fill:#f3e5f5
    style AllNoDims fill:#e8f5e8
```

Sources: [src/units.jl:36-44](), [src/units.jl:46-53](), [src/units.jl:56-59]()

## Boltzmann Constant Handling

Molly.jl provides special handling for the Boltzmann constant, which is essential for temperature coupling and thermodynamic calculations. The system automatically determines the appropriate form of the Boltzmann constant based on the energy units.

### Boltzmann Constant Selection

| Energy Unit Type | Boltzmann Constant Used | Value |
|------------------|-------------------------|--------|
| Molar Energy (`𝐋²⋅𝐌⋅𝐓⁻²⋅𝐍⁻¹`) | `Unitful.k * Unitful.Na` | Gas constant R |
| Non-molar Energy (`𝐋²⋅𝐌⋅𝐓⁻²`) | `Unitful.k` | Boltzmann constant k |
| Unitless (`NoUnits`) | Stripped value | `ustrip(u"u * nm^2 * ps^-2 * K^-1", Unitful.k)` |

The `default_k()` function selects the appropriate Boltzmann constant, while `convert_k_units()` handles unit conversion and validation for user-supplied values.

Sources: [src/units.jl:156-168](), [src/units.jl:172-190]()

## Utility Functions

### Unit Stripping and Conversion

The `ustrip_vec()` function provides a broadcasted version of Unitful's `ustrip()` for efficient unit removal from arrays:

```julia
# Example usage
coordinates_unitless = ustrip_vec.(coordinates)
coordinates_in_nm = ustrip_vec.(u"nm", coordinates)
```

### Energy Unit Conversion

The `energy_remove_mol()` function converts molar energies to per-particle energies by dividing by Avogadro's number. This is useful for certain calculations that require per-particle rather than per-mole quantities.

Sources: [src/units.jl:14-16](), [src/units.jl:206-213]()

## Error Handling and Validation

The unit system provides comprehensive error messages for common unit mismatches:

### Common Error Scenarios

| Error Type | Cause | Error Message Pattern |
|------------|-------|----------------------|
| Mixed Units | Coordinates with different units | "coordinates have mixed units" |
| Molar Inconsistency | Mixing molar and non-molar quantities | "inconsistent energy, force and mass units" |
| Dimension Mismatch | Wrong physical dimensions | "do not have dimensions of energy/mass/etc." |
| Unit Incompatibility | Force/energy unit mismatch | "force_units was specified as X, but that is different from energy_units divided by..." |

The validation functions use `dimension()` from Unitful.jl to check physical dimensions and `unit()` to verify specific unit consistency.

Sources: [src/units.jl:117-123](), [src/units.jl:40-44](), [src/units.jl:56-59]()

## Best Practices

1. **Consistent Unit Sets**: Choose a consistent set of units for your simulation (e.g., nm, ps, u, K, kJ/mol).
2. **Molar vs Non-molar**: Decide whether to use molar quantities throughout or stick to absolute quantities.
3. **Unit Validation**: Let the system validate units during initialization rather than trying to bypass checks.
4. **Default Units**: When in doubt, use the common molecular dynamics units: nm for length, ps for time, u for mass, and kJ/mol for energy.

The unit system in Molly.jl is designed to prevent physical errors while maintaining flexibility for different simulation contexts and unit preferences.

Sources: [src/units.jl:1-214]()

# Page: Data Management

# Data Management

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/analysis.jl](src/analysis.jl)
- [src/loggers.jl](src/loggers.jl)

</details>



Data management in Molly.jl encompasses the collection, storage, analysis, and visualization of simulation data throughout molecular dynamics runs. This system provides comprehensive tools for monitoring simulation properties, recording trajectories, performing post-simulation analysis, and generating output files in various formats.

For detailed information about specific logging mechanisms and analysis functions, see [Logging and Analysis](#8.1). For visualization capabilities and output file formats, see [Visualization and Output](#8.2).

## Data Flow Architecture

The data management system in Molly.jl follows a structured pipeline where simulation data is collected during runtime, processed through analysis tools, and output in various formats.

**Data Flow Through Molly.jl**
```mermaid
graph TD
    Simulation["Simulation Loop<br/>VelocityVerlet, Langevin"] --> LoggerApplication["apply_loggers!<br/>Data Collection"]
    
    LoggerApplication --> PropertyLoggers["Property Loggers<br/>Temperature, Energy, Forces"]
    LoggerApplication --> TrajectoryLoggers["Trajectory Loggers<br/>Coordinates, Velocities"]
    LoggerApplication --> AnalysisLoggers["Analysis Loggers<br/>Correlation, Averaging"]
    
    PropertyLoggers --> InMemoryStorage["In-Memory Storage<br/>Vector{T}, CircularBuffer"]
    TrajectoryLoggers --> FileOutput["File Output<br/>PDB, DCD, XTC"]
    AnalysisLoggers --> StatisticalData["Statistical Data<br/>Correlations, Averages"]
    
    InMemoryStorage --> PostAnalysis["Post-Simulation Analysis<br/>displacements, rmsd, rdf"]
    StatisticalData --> PostAnalysis
    
    PostAnalysis --> Visualization["Visualization<br/>GLMakie Integration"]
    PostAnalysis --> Reports["Analysis Reports<br/>Properties, Statistics"]
    
    FileOutput --> ExternalTools["External Analysis<br/>VMD, PyMOL, MDAnalysis"]
```

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:28-47](), [src/analysis.jl:1-11]()

## Logger System Architecture

The logging system is built around a flexible architecture that allows different types of data to be collected at specified intervals during simulation.

**Logger Type Hierarchy**
```mermaid
graph TB
    BaseLogger["Logger Interface<br/>log_property!"]
    
    BaseLogger --> GeneralObservableLogger["GeneralObservableLogger<br/>Generic observable recording"]
    BaseLogger --> SpecializedLoggers["Specialized Loggers"]
    BaseLogger --> FileWriters["File Writers"]
    BaseLogger --> StatisticalLoggers["Statistical Loggers"]
    
    GeneralObservableLogger --> TemperatureLogger["TemperatureLogger<br/>temperature_wrapper"]
    GeneralObservableLogger --> EnergyLoggers["Energy Loggers<br/>KineticEnergyLogger<br/>PotentialEnergyLogger<br/>TotalEnergyLogger"]
    GeneralObservableLogger --> PropertyLoggers["Property Loggers<br/>VolumeLogger<br/>DensityLogger<br/>PressureLogger"]
    
    SpecializedLoggers --> CoordinatesLogger["CoordinatesLogger<br/>coordinates_wrapper"]
    SpecializedLoggers --> VelocitiesLogger["VelocitiesLogger<br/>velocities_wrapper"]
    SpecializedLoggers --> ForcesLogger["ForcesLogger<br/>forces_wrapper"]
    
    FileWriters --> TrajectoryWriter["TrajectoryWriter<br/>Chemfiles, BioStructures"]
    FileWriters --> StructureWriter["StructureWriter<br/>PDB format"]
    
    StatisticalLoggers --> TimeCorrelationLogger["TimeCorrelationLogger<br/>Green-Kubo analysis"]
    StatisticalLoggers --> AverageObservableLogger["AverageObservableLogger<br/>Block averaging"]
    StatisticalLoggers --> ReplicaExchangeLogger["ReplicaExchangeLogger<br/>Exchange statistics"]
    StatisticalLoggers --> MonteCarloLogger["MonteCarloLogger<br/>Acceptance statistics"]
```

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:57-97](), [src/loggers.jl:102-116](), [src/loggers.jl:526-584]()

## Data Collection Mechanisms

### Observable Logging

The core logging mechanism is the `GeneralObservableLogger` which provides a template for recording any system property that can be computed as a function of the system state.

| Logger Type | Observable Function | Data Type | Purpose |
|------------|-------------------|-----------|---------|
| `TemperatureLogger` | `temperature_wrapper` | Energy units | System temperature |
| `KineticEnergyLogger` | `kinetic_energy_wrapper` | Energy units | Kinetic energy |
| `PotentialEnergyLogger` | `potential_energy_wrapper` | Energy units | Potential energy |
| `TotalEnergyLogger` | `total_energy_wrapper` | Energy units | Total system energy |
| `VolumeLogger` | `volume_wrapper` | Volume units | System volume |
| `DensityLogger` | `density_wrapper` | Density units | System density |
| `VirialLogger` | `virial_wrapper` | Energy units | Virial tensor |
| `PressureLogger` | `pressure_wrapper` | Pressure units | System pressure |

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:99-111](), [src/loggers.jl:166-183](), [src/loggers.jl:194-227]()

### Trajectory Recording

Coordinate and velocity data are handled by specialized loggers that store arrays of `SVector` objects representing atomic positions and velocities over time.

```mermaid
graph LR
    SystemState["System State<br/>coords, velocities, forces"] --> DataCapture["Data Capture<br/>coordinates_wrapper<br/>velocities_wrapper<br/>forces_wrapper"]
    
    DataCapture --> MemoryStorage["Memory Storage<br/>Vector{SArray}"]
    DataCapture --> FileStorage["File Storage<br/>TrajectoryWriter"]
    
    FileStorage --> PDBFormat["PDB Format<br/>BioStructures.jl"]
    FileStorage --> OtherFormats["Other Formats<br/>DCD, XTC, TRR<br/>Chemfiles.jl"]
    
    MemoryStorage --> Analysis["In-Memory Analysis<br/>displacements<br/>distances<br/>rmsd"]
```

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:118-141](), [src/loggers.jl:142-164](), [src/loggers.jl:228-258]()

## Statistical Analysis Tools

### Time Correlation Analysis

The `TimeCorrelationLogger` implements Green-Kubo correlation function calculations for transport property estimation.

**Time Correlation Calculation Flow**
```mermaid
graph TD
    ObservableA["Observable A<br/>observableA function"] --> HistoryA["Circular Buffer A<br/>history_A"]
    ObservableB["Observable B<br/>observableB function"] --> HistoryB["Circular Buffer B<br/>history_B"]
    
    HistoryA --> DotProducts["Dot Products<br/>A_t · B_0"]
    HistoryB --> DotProducts
    
    DotProducts --> SumProducts["sum_offset_products<br/>Accumulation"]
    
    ObservableA --> RunningMeans["Running Averages<br/>sum_A, sum_B"]
    ObservableB --> RunningMeans
    
    ObservableA --> RunningSums["Sum of Squares<br/>sum_sq_A, sum_sq_B"]
    ObservableB --> RunningSums
    
    SumProducts --> CorrelationFunction["C(t) = ⟨A_t·B_0⟩ - ⟨A⟩⟨B⟩"]
    RunningMeans --> CorrelationFunction
    RunningSums --> NormalizedCorrelation["Normalized C(t)<br/>/ sqrt(⟨|A|²⟩⟨|B|²⟩)"]
    CorrelationFunction --> NormalizedCorrelation
```

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:644-721](), [src/loggers.jl:748-784](), [src/loggers.jl:786-800]()

### Block Averaging

The `AverageObservableLogger` implements block averaging for statistical error estimation following the Flyvbjerg-Petersen method.

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:802-847](), [src/loggers.jl:849-867]()

## Analysis Functions

Post-simulation analysis tools provide standard molecular dynamics analysis capabilities.

| Function | Purpose | Input | Output |
|----------|---------|-------|---------|
| `displacements` | Pairwise displacement vectors | Coordinates, boundary | Vector array |
| `distances` | Pairwise distance matrix | Coordinates, boundary | Distance matrix |
| `rmsd` | Root-mean-square deviation | Two coordinate sets | Scalar distance |
| `radius_gyration` | Radius of gyration | Coordinates, atoms | Scalar radius |
| `hydrodynamic_radius` | Hydrodynamic radius | Coordinates, boundary | Scalar radius |
| `rdf` | Radial distribution function | Coordinates, boundary | Distance bins, densities |

Sources: [src/analysis.jl:12-96](), [src/analysis.jl:142-152]()

## Integration with Simulation Loop

The logger system integrates seamlessly with the main simulation loop through the `apply_loggers!` function, which is called at each simulation step.

**Logger Execution Control**
```mermaid
graph TD
    SimulationStep["Simulation Step<br/>step_n"] --> ApplyLoggers["apply_loggers!<br/>run_loggers parameter"]
    
    ApplyLoggers --> CheckRunLoggers{"run_loggers?<br/>true/false/:skipzero"}
    
    CheckRunLoggers -->|true| RunAllLoggers["Execute All Loggers"]
    CheckRunLoggers -->|false| SkipLoggers["Skip Logging"]
    CheckRunLoggers -->|:skipzero + step_n=0| SkipFirstStep["Skip First Step Only"]
    CheckRunLoggers -->|:skipzero + step_n>0| RunAllLoggers
    
    RunAllLoggers --> IterateLoggers["For logger in sys.loggers"]
    IterateLoggers --> LogProperty["log_property!<br/>Individual logger execution"]
    
    LogProperty --> CheckNSteps{"step_n % n_steps == 0?"}
    CheckNSteps -->|true| RecordData["Record Observable"]
    CheckNSteps -->|false| SkipRecord["Skip Recording"]
```

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:28-47](), [src/loggers.jl:77-91]()

# Page: Logging and Analysis

# Logging and Analysis

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/analysis.jl](src/analysis.jl)
- [src/loggers.jl](src/loggers.jl)

</details>



This document covers the data collection and analysis capabilities in Molly.jl, including the logging system for recording simulation properties during runtime and post-simulation analysis tools for processing collected data. The logging framework provides both real-time property monitoring and trajectory storage, while analysis functions enable calculation of structural and dynamical properties.

For information about visualization and output file formats, see [Visualization and Output](#8.2). For details about setting up simulations that generate data to log, see [System Setup and Configuration](#7).

## Logging System Architecture

The logging system in Molly.jl is built around a flexible observer pattern that allows properties to be recorded at specified intervals during simulation. The core mechanism uses the `apply_loggers!` function to execute all registered loggers on each simulation step.

### Core Logging Framework

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Simulation Loop"
        SimStep["Simulation Step"]
        ApplyLoggers["apply_loggers!"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Logger Registry"
        SystemLoggers["System.loggers"]
        LoggerDict["Dict{Symbol, Logger}"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Base Logger Types"
        GeneralLogger["GeneralObservableLogger"]
        SpecificLoggers["Specific Loggers<br/>TemperatureLogger<br/>CoordinatesLogger<br/>etc."]
    end
    
    subgraph "Logging Interface"
        LogProperty["log_property!"]
        LoggerHistory["Logger.history"]
        ValuesAccess["values()"]
    end
    
    SimStep --> ApplyLoggers
    ApplyLoggers --> SystemLoggers
    SystemLoggers --> LoggerDict
    LoggerDict --> GeneralLogger
    LoggerDict --> SpecificLoggers
    GeneralLogger --> LogProperty
    SpecificLoggers --> LogProperty
    LogProperty --> LoggerHistory
    LoggerHistory --> ValuesAccess
    
    style ApplyLoggers fill:#f9f9f9
    style GeneralLogger fill:#f9f9f9
    style LogProperty fill:#f9f9f9
```

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:39-47]()

The logging system operates through several key components:

- **`apply_loggers!`**: Central dispatcher that executes all loggers in `system.loggers` [src/loggers.jl:39-47]()
- **`GeneralObservableLogger`**: Base logger type that records arbitrary observable functions [src/loggers.jl:57-65]()
- **`log_property!`**: Interface function that each logger implements to record data [src/loggers.jl:85-91]()

## Built-in Logger Types

Molly.jl provides a comprehensive set of pre-built loggers for common simulation properties:

| Logger Type | Purpose | Data Type | Usage |
|-------------|---------|-----------|--------|
| `TemperatureLogger` | System temperature | Energy units | `TemperatureLogger(n_steps)` |
| `CoordinatesLogger` | Atomic positions | Position vectors | `CoordinatesLogger(n_steps)` |
| `VelocitiesLogger` | Atomic velocities | Velocity vectors | `VelocitiesLogger(n_steps)` |
| `KineticEnergyLogger` | Kinetic energy | Energy units | `KineticEnergyLogger(n_steps)` |
| `PotentialEnergyLogger` | Potential energy | Energy units | `PotentialEnergyLogger(n_steps)` |
| `TotalEnergyLogger` | Total energy | Energy units | `TotalEnergyLogger(n_steps)` |
| `ForcesLogger` | Forces on atoms | Force vectors | `ForcesLogger(n_steps)` |
| `VolumeLogger` | System volume | Volume units | `VolumeLogger(n_steps)` |
| `DensityLogger` | System density | Density units | `DensityLogger(n_steps)` |
| `VirialLogger` | Virial tensor | Energy units | `VirialLogger(n_steps)` |
| `PressureLogger` | System pressure | Pressure units | `PressureLogger(n_steps)` |

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:102-333]()

### Energy and Thermodynamic Loggers

The energy loggers demonstrate the system's optimization for computational efficiency:

- **`PotentialEnergyLogger`**: Can reuse pre-calculated potential energy via `current_potential_energy` parameter [src/loggers.jl:185-192]()
- **`ForcesLogger`**: Can reuse pre-calculated forces via `current_forces` parameter [src/loggers.jl:229-236]()
- **`TotalEnergyLogger`**: Combines kinetic and potential energy calculations [src/loggers.jl:211-213]()

## Statistical and Advanced Loggers

### Time Correlation Analysis

The `TimeCorrelationLogger` provides sophisticated statistical analysis capabilities for computing time correlations between observables:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Time Correlation Workflow"
        ObsA["Observable A<br/>observableA()"]
        ObsB["Observable B<br/>observableB()"]
        History["Circular Buffers<br/>history_A, history_B"]
        Correlation["Correlation Calculation<br/>sum_offset_products"]
        Output["values()<br/>normalize option"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Statistical Accumulation"
        SumA["sum_A"]
        SumB["sum_B"]
        SumSqA["sum_sq_A"]
        SumSqB["sum_sq_B"]
    end
    
    ObsA --> History
    ObsB --> History
    ObsA --> SumA
    ObsB --> SumB
    ObsA --> SumSqA
    ObsB --> SumSqB
    
    History --> Correlation
    SumA --> Output
    SumB --> Output
    SumSqA --> Output
    SumSqB --> Output
    Correlation --> Output
    
    style History fill:#f9f9f9
    style Correlation fill:#f9f9f9
```

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:644-800]()

The `TimeCorrelationLogger` computes normalized correlations of the form:
```
C(t) = ⟨A_t·B_0⟩ - ⟨A⟩·⟨B⟩ / √(⟨|A|²⟩⟨|B|²⟩)
```

### Block Averaging for Error Estimation

The `AverageObservableLogger` implements block averaging for statistical error estimation:

- **Adaptive block sizing**: Automatically doubles block size when buffer fills [src/loggers.jl:861-865]()
- **Memory efficient**: Stores block averages rather than full observation history [src/loggers.jl:824-836]()
- **Error estimation**: Returns both mean and standard deviation via `values(logger; std=true)` [src/loggers.jl:838-847]()

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:802-873]()

## Trajectory and Structure Output

### TrajectoryWriter System

The `TrajectoryWriter` provides comprehensive trajectory output capabilities:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "File Format Support"
        PDB["PDB Format<br/>BioStructures.jl"]
        Chemfiles["Multiple Formats<br/>Chemfiles.jl<br/>DCD, XTC, TRR, etc."]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Selection"
        AtomInds["atom_inds<br/>Subset selection"]
        ExcludedRes["excluded_res<br/>Residue filtering"]
        WriteVel["write_velocities<br/>Optional velocities"]
        WriteBound["write_boundary<br/>Periodic boundaries"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Writing Process"
        Topology["Topology<br/>Bond information"]
        Coordinates["Coordinates<br/>Position data"]
        Frame["Frame Assembly"]
        FileWrite["File Output"]
    end
    
    PDB --> AtomInds
    Chemfiles --> AtomInds
    AtomInds --> Topology
    ExcludedRes --> Topology
    WriteVel --> Coordinates
    WriteBound --> Coordinates
    
    Topology --> Frame
    Coordinates --> Frame
    Frame --> FileWrite
    
    style Frame fill:#f9f9f9
    style FileWrite fill:#f9f9f9
```

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:526-617]()

Key features of trajectory writing:
- **Format detection**: Automatic format detection from file extension [src/loggers.jl:576-581]()
- **Topology calculation**: Optional topology generation from system bond information [src/loggers.jl:408-436]()
- **Unit conversion**: Automatic unit conversion to standard file formats (Å for coordinates) [src/loggers.jl:449-455]()

## Analysis Functions

The analysis module provides post-simulation calculation tools for structural and dynamical properties:

### Structural Analysis Tools

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input Data"
        Coords["Coordinates<br/>coords"]
        Boundary["Boundary<br/>boundary"]
        Atoms["Atoms<br/>atoms"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Distance Calculations"
        Displacements["displacements()"]
        Distances["distances()"]
        PBC["Periodic Boundary<br/>Corrections"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Structural Properties"
        RMSD["rmsd()<br/>Kabsch alignment"]
        RadGyr["radius_gyration()<br/>Mass-weighted"]
        HydroRad["hydrodynamic_radius()<br/>Harmonic mean"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Advanced Analysis"
        RDF["rdf()<br/>Radial distribution"]
        Visualization["visualize()<br/>Animation"]
    end
    
    Coords --> Displacements
    Boundary --> Displacements
    Displacements --> Distances
    Displacements --> PBC
    
    Coords --> RMSD
    Coords --> RadGyr
    Coords --> HydroRad
    Atoms --> RadGyr
    
    Coords --> RDF
    Coords --> Visualization
    Boundary --> RDF
    Boundary --> Visualization
    
    style PBC fill:#f9f9f9
    style RMSD fill:#f9f9f9
```

Sources: [src/analysis.jl:1-153]()

### Key Analysis Functions

**Distance Calculations**: The `displacements` and `distances` functions properly handle periodic boundary conditions [src/analysis.jl:18-32]()

**RMSD Calculation**: Uses the Kabsch algorithm for optimal superimposition of coordinate sets [src/analysis.jl:43-59]()

**Radius of Gyration**: Mass-weighted calculation for polymer and protein analysis [src/analysis.jl:71-77]()

**Hydrodynamic Radius**: Implements the harmonic mean formula for diffusion properties [src/analysis.jl:89-96]()

## Integration with Simulation Workflow

The logging system integrates seamlessly with the simulation loop through the `apply_loggers!` mechanism:

### Logger Execution Control

The `run_loggers` parameter in `apply_loggers!` provides flexible control:
- **`true`**: Always run loggers [src/loggers.jl:41]()
- **`false`**: Skip all loggers [src/loggers.jl:41]()
- **`:skipzero`**: Skip loggers on step 0 [src/loggers.jl:41]()

### Performance Considerations

- **Automatic differentiation**: Loggers are ignored during gradient calculations [src/loggers.jl:37]()
- **Threading support**: Multi-threaded execution for computationally expensive loggers [src/loggers.jl:40]()
- **Memory efficiency**: Circular buffers prevent unlimited memory growth in correlation loggers [src/loggers.jl:687-688]()

### Specialized Simulation Loggers

**ReplicaExchangeLogger**: Tracks exchange attempts and success rates in replica exchange simulations [src/loggers.jl:875-920]()

**MonteCarloLogger**: Records acceptance rates and energy statistics for Monte Carlo methods [src/loggers.jl:921-956]()

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:39-47](), [src/loggers.jl:875-956]()

# Visualization and Output

<details>

This page covers the data export and visualization capabilities in Molly.jl, including writing trajectory files, creating structure outputs, and generating visual representations of molecular dynamics simulations. For information about data collection during simulations, see [Logging and Analysis](#8.1).

## File Output System

Molly.jl provides comprehensive file writing capabilities through two main approaches: direct structure writing and trajectory logging during simulations.

### Structure Writing

The `write_structure` function provides one-time structure output to various file formats:

```mermaid
graph TD
    WriteStructure["write_structure()"] --> FormatDetection["Format Detection"]
    FormatDetection --> PDBPath["PDB Format"]
    FormatDetection --> ChemfilesPath["Other Formats"]
    
    PDBPath --> BioStructures["BioStructures.jl"]
    ChemfilesPath --> Chemfiles["Chemfiles.jl"]
    
    BioStructures --> PDBOutput["PDB Files<br/>(.pdb)"]
    Chemfiles --> MultiFormat["Multiple Formats<br/>DCD, XTC, CIF, MOL2<br/>SDF, TRR, XYZ"]
    
    WriteStructure --> SystemData["System Data"]
    SystemData --> AtomsData["atoms_data"]
    SystemData --> Topology["topology"]
    SystemData --> Coordinates["coords"]
    SystemData --> Boundary["boundary"]
```

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:479-524]()

### Trajectory Writers

The `TrajectoryWriter` logger enables continuous output during simulations:

```mermaid
graph LR
    TrajectoryWriter --> Configuration["Configuration"]
    Configuration --> FilePath["filepath"]
    Configuration --> Format["format"]
    Configuration --> AtomSelection["atom_inds"]
    Configuration --> ExcludedRes["excluded_res"]

    Configuration --> WriteBoundary["write_boundary"]
    
    TrajectoryWriter --> OutputMethods["Output Methods"]
    OutputMethods --> PDBMethod["PDB Method<br/>write_pdb_coords()"]
    OutputMethods --> ChemfilesMethod["Chemfiles Method<br/>write_chemfiles!()"]
    
    PDBMethod --> PDBTrajectory["Multi-model PDB<br/>MODEL/ENDMDL records"]
    ChemfilesMethod --> BinaryTrajectory["Binary Trajectories<br/>DCD, XTC, TRR"]
```

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:526-617]()

## Supported File Formats

Molly.jl supports a wide range of molecular file formats through integration with established Julia packages:

| Format | Extension | Library | Coordinates | Velocities | Topology | Notes |
|--------|-----------|---------|-------------|------------|----------|-------|
| PDB | `.pdb` | BioStructures.jl | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | Special handling for residue info |
| DCD | `.dcd` | Chemfiles.jl | ✓ | ✓* | ✗ | Binary trajectory format |
| XTC | `.xtc` | Chemfiles.jl | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | Compressed trajectory |
| TRR | `.trr` | Chemfiles.jl | ✓ | ✓* | ✗ | Full precision trajectory |
| CIF | `.cif` | Chemfiles.jl | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | Crystallographic format |
| MOL2 | `.mol2` | Chemfiles.jl | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | Tripos format |
| SDF | `.sdf` | Chemfiles.jl | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | Structure data format |
| XYZ | `.xyz` | Chemfiles.jl | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | Simple coordinate format |

*Velocity support depends on format capabilities

Sources: [src/loggers.jl:488-489](), [src/loggers.jl:533-537]()

# Page: Development and Testing

# Development and Testing

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [test/runtests.jl](test/runtests.jl)
- [test/simulation.jl](test/simulation.jl)

</details>



This page covers the testing framework, development practices, and contribution guidelines for Molly.jl. It details how the comprehensive test suite is organized, how tests are executed across different hardware backends, and the benchmarking infrastructure used to ensure performance and correctness.

For information about specific simulation algorithms and their implementation, see [Simulation Engine](#5). For details about GPU acceleration features, see [GPU Acceleration](#6.1).

## Test Framework Organization

Molly.jl uses a comprehensive testing framework built on Julia's standard `Test` package, organized into several categories based on functionality and computational requirements.

### Test Categories

The test suite is divided into logical groups that can be run independently or together:

| Test Group | Purpose | Key Files |
|------------|---------|-----------|
| Basic | Core data structures and utilities | `test/basic.jl` |
| Interactions | Force calculations and energy functions | `test/interactions.jl` |
| Simulation | Integration algorithms and dynamics | `test/simulation.jl` |
| Protein | Biomolecular force fields and structures | `test/protein.jl` |
| Gradients | Automatic differentiation functionality | `test/gradients.jl` |
| Minimization | Energy minimization algorithms | `test/minimization.jl` |
| Agent | Agent-based modeling features | `test/agent.jl` |

```mermaid
graph TB
    MainRunner["test/runtests.jl<br/>Main Test Runner"]
    
    subgraph "Core Tests"
        Basic["test/basic.jl<br/>Basic Functionality"]
```

Sources: [test/runtests.jl:30-35](), [test/runtests.jl:113-136]()

### Test Selection and Configuration

Tests can be selectively executed using environment variables:

- `GROUP` - Controls which test categories to run (`All`, `Protein`, `Gradients`, `NotGradients`)
- `GPUTESTS` - Enables or disables GPU testing (`0` to disable, `1` to enable)
- `VISTESTS` - Controls visualization tests (`0` to disable, `1` to enable)
- `DEVICE` - Specifies which GPU device to use for testing

Sources: [test/runtests.jl:30-35](), [test/runtests.jl:43-48](), [test/runtests.jl:58-61]()

## Testing Infrastructure and Hardware Support

The testing framework supports multiple hardware backends and array types to ensure compatibility across different computational environments.

### Hardware Backend Testing Matrix

```mermaid
graph LR
```

### GPU Testing Configuration

The framework automatically detects available GPU backends and configures testing accordingly:

```julia
const run_cuda_tests   = run_gpu_tests && CUDA.functional()
const run_rocm_tests   = run_gpu_tests && AMDGPU.functional()
const run_oneapi_tests = run_gpu_tests && oneAPI.functional()
const run_metal_tests  = run_gpu_tests && Metal.functional()
```

Each GPU backend is tested with appropriate array types and precision levels. CUDA supports both Float32 and Float64, while other backends primarily use Float32 for optimal performance.

Sources: [test/runtests.jl:62-65](), [test/runtests.jl:69-98]()

## Simulation Testing Framework

The simulation tests form the core of the testing infrastructure, validating molecular dynamics algorithms across different scenarios and hardware configurations.

### Key Test Scenarios

The simulation test suite covers a comprehensive range of molecular dynamics scenarios:

| Test Set | System Size | Duration | Key Features |
|----------|-------------|----------|--------------|
| Lennard-Jones 2D | 10 atoms | 20,000 steps | 2D boundary conditions, temperature control |
| Lennard-Jones 3D | 100 atoms | 20,000 steps | Full 3D simulation, multiple loggers |
| Infinite Boundaries | 100 atoms | 2,000 steps | Non-periodic boundary conditions |
| Different Simulators | 100 atoms | 20,000 steps | Verlet, Langevin, OverdampedLangevin |
| Pairwise Interactions | 100 atoms | 20,000 steps | LJ, Coulomb, SoftSphere, Mie potentials |
| Constraints | 400 atoms | 10,000 steps | SHAKE/RATTLE algorithms |
| REMD | 100 atoms | 10,000 steps | Temperature and Hamiltonian exchange |

### Cross-Platform Validation

A critical aspect of the testing framework is ensuring identical results across different hardware backends and precision levels:

```mermaid
graph TD
    RefRun["Reference Run<br/>(CPU, Float64)"]
    
    subgraph "Test Runs"
        CPUf32["CPU Float32"]
        CUDA["CUDA GPU"]

        Metal["Metal GPU"]
        OneAPI["OneAPI GPU"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Validation Metrics"
        CoordDiff["Coordinate Difference<br/>< 1e-4 nm"]
        EnergyDiff["Energy Difference<br/>< 5e-4 kJ/mol"]
    end
    
    RefRun --> CPUf32
    RefRun --> CUDA
    RefRun --> ROCm
    RefRun --> Metal
    RefRun --> OneAPI
    
    CPUf32 --> CoordDiff
    CPUf32 --> EnergyDiff
    CUDA --> CoordDiff
    CUDA --> EnergyDiff
    ROCm --> CoordDiff
    ROCm --> EnergyDiff
    Metal --> CoordDiff
    Metal --> EnergyDiff
    OneAPI --> CoordDiff
    OneAPI --> EnergyDiff
```

Sources: [test/simulation.jl:1483-1494]()

### Test System Generation

The framework includes utilities for generating test systems with controlled properties:

- `place_atoms()` - Generates random atomic positions with minimum distance constraints
- `place_diatomics()` - Creates diatomic molecule configurations
- `random_velocity()` - Generates Maxwell-Boltzmann distributed velocities
- Crystal structures via `SimpleCrystals.jl` integration

Sources: [test/simulation.jl:24-27](), [test/simulation.jl:1390-1393](), [test/simulation.jl:1322-1325]()

## Performance Benchmarking and Validation

### Timing and Performance Metrics

Test execution includes timing measurements to monitor performance across different implementations:

```julia
@time simulate!(s, simulator, n_steps; n_threads=n_threads)
```

The framework tracks:
- Simulation step timing
- Force calculation performance
- Neighbor list construction time
- Memory allocation patterns
- GPU kernel execution times

### Correctness Validation

Multiple validation approaches ensure simulation correctness:

1. **Energy Conservation** - Monitoring total energy drift in NVE simulations
2. **Temperature Control** - Validating thermostat effectiveness
3. **Structural Properties** - Checking radial distribution functions and bond lengths
4. **Statistical Mechanics** - Verifying ensemble averages match theoretical predictions

Sources: [test/simulation.jl:188](), [test/simulation.jl:474]()

### Special CI Considerations

The CI environment has specific configurations to handle resource constraints:

- CPU gradient tests are limited due to memory constraints
- GPU tests run only when appropriate hardware is available
- Visualization tests are disabled by default
- Long-running tests use reduced step counts

Sources: [test/runtests.jl:37-41]()

### Code Quality Assurance

The framework integrates several quality assurance tools:

- **Aqua.jl** - Detects common package issues like method ambiguities and unbound arguments
- **Coverage analysis** - Monitors test coverage across the codebase
- **Formatting checks** - Ensures consistent code style
- **Dependency analysis** - Validates package dependencies and load times

Sources: [test/runtests.jl:114-121]()

## Development Workflow and Contributing

### Running Tests Locally

Developers can run specific test categories:

```julia
# Run all tests
julia test/runtests.jl

# Run only simulation tests  
GROUP="NotGradients" julia test/runtests.jl

# Run with GPU tests disabled
GPUTESTS="0" julia test/runtests.jl

# Run on specific GPU device
DEVICE="1" julia test/runtests.jl
```

### Adding New Tests

When contributing new functionality:

1. **Add unit tests** in the appropriate test file
2. **Include cross-platform validation** for GPU-compatible features  
3. **Add performance benchmarks** for computationally intensive functions
4. **Test multiple precision levels** (Float32/Float64) where applicable
5. **Validate against reference implementations** when available

### Test Data and Resources

The testing framework uses standardized test data:

- Force field files in `data/force_fields/`
- Molecular structures in `data/openmm_6mrr/`
- Reference simulation data for validation
- Temporary files for I/O testing

Sources: [test/runtests.jl:100-109]()

# Page: Testing Framework

# Testing Framework

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [test/basic.jl](test/basic.jl)
- [test/energy_conservation.jl](test/energy_conservation.jl)
- [test/protein.jl](test/protein.jl)
- [test/runtests.jl](test/runtests.jl)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The testing framework in Molly.jl provides comprehensive validation of molecular dynamics functionality across different hardware platforms, numerical precision levels, and use cases. This framework ensures correctness, performance, and compatibility of simulations on CPU and GPU architectures while maintaining numerical accuracy and energy conservation properties.

For information about performance benchmarking and optimization strategies, see [Benchmarking and Performance](#9.2).

## Test Organization and Structure

The test suite is organized into specialized test files that cover different aspects of the molecular dynamics package:

```mermaid
graph TD
    runtests["runtests.jl<br/>Main test runner"]
    basic["basic.jl<br/>Core functionality"]
    protein["protein.jl<br/>Protein systems"]
    interactions["interactions.jl<br/>Force calculations"]
    simulation["simulation.jl<br/>Integration methods"]
    gradients["gradients.jl<br/>Differentiable MD"]
    agent["agent.jl<br/>Agent-based modeling"]
    minimization["minimization.jl<br/>Energy minimization"]
    energy_conservation["energy_conservation.jl<br/>Energy conservation"]
    
    runtests --> basic
    runtests --> protein
    runtests --> interactions
    runtests --> simulation
    runtests --> gradients
    runtests --> agent
    runtests --> minimization
    runtests --> energy_conservation
    
    basic --> spatial["Spatial calculations"]
    basic --> neighbors["Neighbor finding"]
    basic --> analysis["Analysis functions"]
    basic --> replica["Replica systems"]
    
    protein --> peptide["Peptide simulations"]
    protein --> openmm["OpenMM comparisons"]
    protein --> implicit["Implicit solvent"]
```

The main test runner coordinates execution based on environment variables and available hardware capabilities.

Sources: [test/runtests.jl:1-136](), [test/basic.jl:1-524](), [test/protein.jl:1-298]()

## Test Groups and Conditional Execution

Tests are organized into groups that can be selectively executed based on the `GROUP` environment variable:

| Group | Description | Files Included |
|-------|-------------|----------------|
| `All` | Complete test suite | All test files |
| `Protein` | Protein-specific tests | `protein.jl` |
| `Gradients` | Differentiable simulation tests | `gradients.jl` |
| `NotGradients` | All tests except gradients | `basic.jl`, `interactions.jl`, `simulation.jl`, `agent.jl`, `minimization.jl`, `protein.jl` |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    start["Test Execution Start"]
    group_check{"GROUP environment<br/>variable check"}
    all_tests["All Tests<br/>GROUP = 'All'"]
    protein_tests["Protein Tests<br/>GROUP = 'Protein'"]
    gradient_tests["Gradient Tests<br/>GROUP = 'Gradients'"]
    no_gradient_tests["Non-Gradient Tests<br/>GROUP = 'NotGradients'"]
    error["Error:<br/>Unrecognized GROUP"]
    
    start --> group_check
    group_check --> |"All"| all_tests
    group_check --> |"Protein"| protein_tests
    group_check --> |"Gradients"| gradient_tests
    group_check --> |"NotGradients"| no_gradient_tests
    group_check --> |"Other"| error
    
    all_tests --> aqua["Aqua.jl quality checks"]
    all_tests --> basic_tests["basic.jl"]
    all_tests --> other_tests["Other test files"]
```

Sources: [test/runtests.jl:29-35](), [test/runtests.jl:113-136]()

## Hardware Platform Testing

The testing framework supports multiple hardware platforms and array types through conditional execution based on hardware availability:

### CPU Testing
- **Single-threaded**: Always available with `Array` type
- **Multi-threaded**: Conditional on `Threads.nthreads() > 1`
- **Parallel tests**: Executed when Julia runs with multiple threads

### GPU Testing
GPU tests are controlled by the `GPUTESTS` environment variable and hardware availability:

```mermaid
graph TD
    gpu_check["GPU Tests Enabled?<br/>GPUTESTS != '0'"]
    
    subgraph "GPU Platform Detection"
        cuda_check["CUDA.functional()"]
        rocm_check["AMDGPU.functional()"]
        oneapi_check["oneAPI.functional()"]
        metal_check["Metal.functional()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Array Types"
        cpu_array["Array<br/>(CPU)"]
        cu_array["CuArray<br/>(NVIDIA)"]
        roc_array["ROCArray<br/>(AMD)"]
        one_array["oneArray<br/>(Intel)"]
        metal_array["MtlArray<br/>(Apple)"]
    end
    
    gpu_check --> cuda_check
    gpu_check --> rocm_check
    gpu_check --> oneapi_check
    gpu_check --> metal_check
    
    cuda_check --> |"Available"| cu_array
    rocm_check --> |"Available"| roc_array
    oneapi_check --> |"Available"| one_array
    metal_check --> |"Available"| metal_array
    
    cpu_array --> test_execution["Test Execution<br/>on Platform"]
    cu_array --> test_execution
    roc_array --> test_execution
    one_array --> test_execution
    metal_array --> test_execution
```

The framework maintains an `array_list` tuple that contains all available array types for testing across platforms.

Sources: [test/runtests.jl:58-98](), [test/runtests.jl:67-98]()

## Test Environment Configuration

### Environment Variables
Key environment variables control test behavior:

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `GROUP` | `"All"` | Selects test group to run |
| `GPUTESTS` | `"1"` | Enables/disables GPU tests |
| `DEVICE` | `"0"` | Specifies GPU device number |
| `VISTESTS` | `"1"` | Enables/disables visualization tests |
| `CI` | - | Indicates CI environment (affects memory-intensive tests) |

### CI-Specific Behavior
Tests adapt to CI environments to handle memory constraints:

```julia
const running_CI = haskey(ENV, "CI")
if running_CI
    @warn "Some CPU gradient tests will not be run as this is CI"
end
```

Sources: [test/runtests.jl:37-41](), [test/runtests.jl:29-35](), [test/runtests.jl:58-61]()

## Core Test Categories

### Spatial and Boundary Tests
Tests for coordinate systems, periodic boundaries, and spatial utility functions:

```mermaid

```

Sources: [test/basic.jl:1-216]()

### Neighbor Finding Tests
Comprehensive testing of neighbor finding algorithms:

- **DistanceNeighborFinder**: Brute force O(N²) algorithm
- **TreeNeighborFinder**: Tree-based spatial partitioning
- **CellListMapNeighborFinder**: Cell list algorithm
- **GPUNeighborFinder**: GPU-optimized neighbor finding

Tests verify consistency across different algorithms and hardware platforms.

Sources: [test/basic.jl:218-338]()

### Protein System Tests
Complex molecular system validation including:

- **Peptide simulations**: Small protein systems with full force fields
- **OpenMM comparisons**: Force and energy validation against OpenMM reference
- **Implicit solvent**: OBC2 and GBN2 implicit solvent models
- **Multi-precision**: Float32 and Float64 testing

Sources: [test/protein.jl:1-298]()

## External Integration Testing

### AtomsBase.jl Integration
Tests conversion between Molly systems and AtomsBase standard:

```julia
# AtomsBase conversion testing
ab_sys = make_test_system().system
molly_sys = System(ab_sys; energy_units=u"kJ", force_units=u"kJ/Å")
test_approx_eq(ab_sys, molly_sys; common_only=true)
```

### AtomsCalculators.jl Interface
Validates calculator interface compliance:

```julia
calc = MollyCalculator(pairwise_inters=(coul,), force_units=u"kJ/Å", energy_units=u"kJ")
pe = AtomsCalculators.potential_energy(ab_sys, calc)
fs = AtomsCalculators.forces(ab_sys, calc)
```

Sources: [test/basic.jl:483-523]()
